chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who believe, but only over those who take him as an ally.

key_terms.يَتَوَلَّوْنَهُ: They take him as an ally/guardian

ai.seo_question: Who does Satan have authority over according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (a) clarification that Satan’s *sultan* (authority/power) is conditional, applying only to those who voluntarily align with him as *awliya'* (allies), rather than being absolute over all believers. This distinction underscores the Shia theological principle of human free will (*ikhtiyar*) and refutes the notion of deterministic predestination regarding sin, emphasizing that obedience to Satan is a choice that can be reversed through divine grace and conscious adherence to the Imams.
